config.grain_rationale: Each row is one name-history entry for one ASIC-registered company: the same ACN repeats across rows when a company has changed name (a current-name row with Current Name Indicator=Y and blank Current Name, plus former-name rows whose separate Current Name column holds the current legal name). Mapped targets are the business participant's attributes (legal name, ACN, ABN, status, type, registration date).

record_id.rationale: ACN is not unique per record (471 distinct ACNs over 473 profiled rows; the same ACN repeats on current-name and former-name rows). No column identifies a row, so content_hash is used.

fields.rationale: Publisher help file: on the row that carries no separate Current Name (the current-name row, indicator=Y), Company Name is the company's current registered legal name. Current Name Start Date is attached as that claim's start where present (usually blank on these rows, giving a null valid_from rather than a guess). Values are right-padded, so collapse_whitespace then trim.

Help file: on a history row the Current Name column holds the company's current legal name and Current Name Start Date dates the start of that name (day-first, e.g. 28/01/2016). That start is the only validity bound the source states for the current name.

Help file: where a row carries a separate Current Name, the Company Name on that row is a former registered name, so scope former_legal_name with no validity bounds - the extract does not establish when a former name stopped being valid. The condition is a value test on the name columns rather than the fragile Y/blank indicator.
Column named ACN, 9-digit shape on 473/473 profiled rows, checksum-valid on 100% of values; use the acn transform.
Help file: ABN '0' is a missing value (145/473 discovery rows). null_if runs before the checksum-validating abn transform; the remaining 11-digit values validate (69.3% of rows emitted).

Help file: REGD registered, DRGD deregistered, EXAD covers BOTH receivership and liquidation, SOFF is strike-off action in progress. REGD->active and DRGD->deregistered are exact. EXAD is mapped explicitly to unknown rather than in_liquidation, because a receivership-only company is not in liquidation and the code cannot establish which applies. SOFF is mapped explicitly to unknown because the company is still registered while strike-off action is in progress and no canonical value fits. Both are stated explicitly rather than silently defaulted.

Type states the ASIC company type explicitly: APTY Australian proprietary company, APUB Australian public company (both profiled, including the LMGT/APUB rows). Both are companies; unlisted codes default to unknown.
Help file: company registration event with day-first dates; all 473 profiled values match 99/99/9999 and held-out values parsed correctly.

constants.rationale: ASIC is the Australian register; every record is an Australian-registered body. No address columns exist, so only the country is defensible.

unmapped.reason: Row-level flag duplicating the name-column pattern (Y rows carry the current name in Company Name with Current Name blank); conditions are taken from the name columns themselves, so the flag is not an entity attribute.
Dates the current-name claim only; used as valid_from_path on both current-name rules, not a standalone entity date.
ASIC internal class code (LMSH limited by shares, LMGT limited by guarantee); no canonical target and no entity_type evidence beyond 'company'.
ASIC sub-class code (PROP/PSTC/LISN/ULSN...); no canonical target.
Historical jurisdiction of registration, not the entity's current address; mapping it to address.state would assert a current location the register does not establish.
State-level registration number (mixed alphanumeric, padded); not an ACN/ABN/NZBN and the ontology has no field for it.
Empty in every profiled row (present_rate 0.0); carries no information.

Dates the end of the company registration, not the validity of any name/type/address claim; using it as valid_to would wrongly end the row's name claim and the engine ignores legacy observation.valid_to for entity history. The deregistered fact is carried by entity.status.

config.notes: Reader settings from evidence: zip member COMPANY_202611.csv, utf-8-sig (BOM), tab-delimited (14 tabs per line; commas occur only inside names), no title rows. Legal names are split per the publisher help file into three complementary rules so every row yields a name: Company Name is the current legal name when no Current Name is carried on the row; Current Name is the current legal name on history rows (dated by Current Name Start Date); and Company Name on those history rows is a former legal name with no validity bounds. Dry run: 473/473 records with output, zero field errors, and 100% of rows now produce a legal_name (636 current from Company Name, 364 current from Current Name, plus 364 former-name observations). entity.status: EXAD (receivership OR liquidation) and SOFF (strike-off in progress) are mapped explicitly to unknown rather than asserting a liquidation or deregistration the source cannot establish. No address columns exist beyond the AU country constant. Record grain is the row (company name-history entry), so record_id is a content hash rather than ACN.
